**Conversation overview**

This was chat 14 of an ongoing multi-session book editing project called "The Method 1.6," a technical volume accompanied by a Register of 1,447 headings (1,472 distinct numbers, range 165–1768), four compendia, two papers, and supporting instruments. The person is the author and sole decision-maker; Claude functions as the editorial executor. The session operated under a strict protocol: the Prime Handoff Directive (hand off at 90% context), the Prime Zeno Directive (fetch → read → analyse → close flags → report; close each segment before the next), and a reading gate requiring all prior chat summaries to be read from files before any work begins. The session opened by executing §0 of HANDOFF-15, printing a certificate confirming 13 chats read, bundle counts, ruling count, Register state, and instrument inventory.

The main substantive work was executing §5 of HANDOFF-15: resolving 66 citation sites pointing to entries excised in chat 12 under Ruling 27. Claude found HANDOFF-15's site list wrong on two counts — stale line numbers (W-001 had shifted the main volume) and short by twelve entries — and re-derived an authoritative list of 40 dangling entries across 97 sites. When the repair required editing live Register entry bodies (a standing prohibition), the person ruled verbatim: remove the pointers, keep the clause content, sweep prose coherence later in one pass — recorded as Ruling 29 and applied as W-002. Claude's instrument `depoint.py` removed 77 explicit pointers (MAIN 21, Register 49, Math 3, Physics 2, Spectra 2), verified by markup-parity checks and a confirmed zero loss of citations to live entries. Downstream stale counts (citation totals in the Register and main volume, the load-bearing table, the build stamp) were corrected. The bundler `bundle.py` was written for the first time and both BUILD-15 bundles were produced and verified by round-trip.

At the close, the person asked for an honest reader's view of Appendix F's purpose. After Claude read it and explained it, the person observed that the Register compendia appeared to supersede it. Claude offered the analysis that Appendix F predates the Ruling 27 Amendment and is the largest surviving instance of the editorial self-audit class that ruling excised — it indexes the book's own printed numbers and reports how well the book verified itself, which is irrelevant to a reader under the amendment. The person ruled verbatim (Ruling 30): remove Appendix F completely without objection, leave a placeholder so no reference to it triggers a fault, and schedule the full rebuild between the edit and audit phases. Claude measured the appendix's extent (290 lines), the 79 external references that must not fault, and the four reference shapes the placeholder must satisfy, then built all of this into HANDOFF-16 with explicit instructions that chat 15 is not to re-argue the ruling. The two structural seeds worth carrying into the eventual rebuild — F.2's four-coordinate index construction and F.3.3's argument about self-count instability — were named in the handoff so they are not lost, with a clear instruction that they are not to be salvaged into the placeholder. Appendix F's removal is item 0 for chat 15, before the press, so the press runs once on the corrected book.

Key standing rules carried forward: entry bodies are never edited (except for the Ruling 29 pointer-removal class); ranges naming spans are not split; prose coherence is not repaired site by site; `guard.py` does not exist and is not rebuilt; the 1,447/1,472 count question is held at PR1; the 126 Spectra rows and five narrow-bracket FAIL rows do not start without a ruling; Ruling 29's coherence sweep is the author's, later, in one pass.

"press both papers" leave the work list as separate-volume tasks.

## RULING 27 — AMENDMENT (author, chat 12, verbatim)
"or the truth of a number the books state - these too must be removed. They too are irrelevant"
Operative: verification of the books' OWN PRINTED NUMBERS (captions vs plots, counts vs counts,
stale figures, corrections owed, internal consistency) is EDITORIAL and is excised.
Verification of a PHYSICAL or MATHEMATICAL result against the world (literature, measurement,
computation) is SUBJECT MATTER and is kept.

## ENTRIES


<!-- EXCISED 190 : A-production -->
### 190

**A SYMBOL THAT NEVER PRINTED.** *The recovery operator ℛ uses U+1D4E1 and the diagnostic operator ⅅ uses U+1D49F. No DejaVu face carries either. Every render of this book placed a blank box instead — 107 of them across 44 pages — and every audit then defined passed, because every one read the source. §3's ARTEFACT audit exists because of this entry.*


<!-- EXCISED 196 : C-internal -->
### 196

**A STATUS TABLE TWO REVISIONS STALE.** *§32.3 still read "nine literatures entered, nine named and unentered" and "order recovery beyond trees: open". Both superseded the same day.*


<!-- EXCISED 199 : C-internal -->
### 199

**FOUR CROSS-REFERENCES IN THE SHIPPED BUILD — THE PREFACE TWICE DIRECTING THE WITHDRAWALS TO CHAPTER 27, THE CONSEQUENCES TO "CHAPTERS 8 TO 10", AND CHAPTER 14 CITING "THEOREM 7.1" — STALE AGAINST THE RENUMBERING THEY SURVIVED.** *The §28.1 pattern at the navigation layer; all four repaired.*


<!-- EXCISED 202 : B-session -->
### 202

**THE TOWER SESSION'S THREE ENTRIES WRITTEN IN UNDER A SECTION NUMBER ALREADY IN USE — A SECOND 21.8 — AND ANCHORED BEFORE 21.7, OUT OF SEQUENCE.** *The §28.1 pattern at the structural layer: an insertion asserted correct against a numbering it had not read. Renumbered 21.7.6 and relocated.*


<!-- EXCISED 204 : C-internal -->
### 204

**FOUR FIGURE CAPTIONS WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIGURES WERE READ; TWO MISDESCRIBED WHAT THEY SHOWED.** *Recaptioned from the rendered images.*


<!-- EXCISED 272 : A-production -->
### 272

**THE PRESS CARRIES HARDCODED COPIES OF THE TITLE PAGES** *, so source and artefact disagreed silently. Both instances repaired; the class was not, and it recurred at register 336.*


<!-- EXCISED 324 : A-production -->
### 324

**THE CONTENTS CARRIED FOUR TIERS WHERE A BOOK NEEDS TWO — AND APPENDIX HEADINGS RENDERED AT 7.6pt, SMALLER THAN THE BODY, BECAUSE THE PRESS READ ONLY HASH-PREFIXED LINES AS HEADINGS.** **A contents may only be shortened where the body can be navigated without it* **, and it could not.*


<!-- EXCISED 341 : A-production -->
### 341

**TWO CHAPTER ONES.** *Part I's sections rendered at chapter tier while numbered as sections. The book now numbers continuously, Part I holding 1–5 and Parts II–V 6–30 — 1,183 edits, and four audits failed after it, all four instruments trailing the book.*


<!-- EXCISED 206,210,269 : C-internal -->
### 206, 210, 269

**STALE FIGURES LEFT BEHIND THEIR OWN CORRECTION.** *Two counts left by a sweep that matched only the phrasings it expected; Appendix D asserting a total its own table contradicted; that table still printing the old total four entries after the correction. Three instances: a correction stated near a table is not a corrected table.*


<!-- EXCISED 260,264 : A-production -->
### 260, 264

**MARKUP THAT OPENED IN ONE UNIT AND CLOSED IN ANOTHER.** *Emphasis straddling a table cell, then a line break inside a callout. Two instances; the press now escapes and joins before parsing emphasis, in both.*


<!-- EXCISED 287,344,358 : C-internal -->
### 287, 344, 358

**A FIGURE STALE AFTER THE CORRECTION THAT SUPERSEDED IT.** *A heading claiming three entries and holding eighty-six; three live present-tense statements a later entry had resolved; a price and its percentage that were one measurement written twice.* **A correction stated near a figure is not a corrected figure.**


<!-- EXCISED 363 : A-production -->
### 363

**THE REGISTER COMPRESSED ENTRY BY ENTRY, IN FIVE BOUNDED PASSES, AND THE COMPRESSION WAS A REWRITE RATHER THAN A TRANSFORM — §2.19's THIRD CONDITION FORBIDS DOING THAT MECHANICALLY, AND A MECHANICAL RULE TESTED EARLIER DESTROYED FINDINGS.** *119 entries carrying 15,278 words become 4,266. What each keeps is its defect and its resolution; what each loses is the reasoning,* **because the reasoning lives in the section the entry cites* **. Register 224 is the test: 148 words to 38, and nothing gone that §29.11 does not hold in full. A dozen kept their length because they carry the finding rather than pointing at it.* **The register falls from 25.0% of the book to 15.9%* **, and the withdrawal ratio of F.4.1 from 0.445 to 0.249. And four register entries were found citing one section where they meant four — the title-based remap of register 354 was right about the sections and wrong about entries written under an earlier numbering.* **A remap keyed on titles fixes the headings and not the history.**


<!-- EXCISED 366 : C-internal -->
### 366

**THE STATED E FOR THE NUMBERS INDEX WAS STALE; RECOMPUTED IT IS 38** *, the book having grown from 2,453 claim-bearing occurrences to 3,183 since the figure was taken. Item M attempted by its second route — the constraint §12's loop offers — and* **the route is refuted* **: a recomputed number ought to carry a stated definition and enumerated inputs, and* **cells the book already occupies contradict both* **, four recording a recomputation whose definition is only asserted and three whose inputs are only named. The constraint cannot be added without withdrawing occupied cells.* **Those seven are the finding a failed route leaves behind* **: a recomputation whose definition is not stated is not checkable, and the book prints seven. Item M stays open with its figure corrected and one of its two routes closed.*


<!-- EXCISED 369 : A-production -->
### 369

**THE SOURCE WAS CORRUPTED TO 25.8 MILLION CHARACTERS — FORTY-FOUR TIMES ITS SIZE — AND THE BUILD, THE AUDITS AND THE DELIVERED COPY ALL PASSED ON IT.** *A block of 1,819 characters in Appendix F stood repeated 13,866 times; the press rendered it, the twenty audits reported clean, and I copied it to the outputs. Found only because the PDF weighed 20 MB and the tripwire count jumped sixfold —* **two figures nothing checks, noticed by eye.** *Repaired by deduplication, with Appendix F spliced from the backup taken before the compression and its E(G) work re-applied. §2.19's fourth condition is why that cost an hour instead of the session.* **No audit measures the size of the artefact it audits* **, and one now should.*


<!-- EXCISED 411 : B-session -->
### 411

**THREE VERIFICATIONS OF MINE WERE WRONG IN ONE SESSION AND THE BOOK WAS RIGHT EVERY TIME** *: the tree cut taken on coordinate order, Aitken indexed from the wrong end of its triple, and an invariant checker reading the wrong table* *while executing §2.19's own condition (v)**. §3.4 records the same thing happening twice to the whitespace audit.* **An audit is not exempt from the discipline it enforces* **, and §4.1 — attribute inward first — earned its place three times over.*


<!-- EXCISED 430 : A-production -->
### 430

**THE PRESS WILL SILENTLY DROP A FIGURE WHOSE NEIGHBOUR SHARES ITS DIMENSIONS** *, and this book contains the case: Figures 16.3 and 16.4 are distinct and both 1560 × 660, so the pairing pass that collapses duplicates would keep one and fail its own assertion at twenty-seven. The heuristic assumes* *equal dimensions implies duplicate* *and has never fired because the original figure directory carried both members of every genuine pair.* **A rule that has never been shown capable of being wrong* **, which is §4.6, found by rebuilding the figures from the artefact rather than by reading the press. The pairing now tests ink variance as well as dimension.*


<!-- EXCISED 431 : A-production -->
### 431

**TWO OF THE SIX BUILD-TIME READOUTS CANNOT RUN.** *§2.21 requires a withdrawn figure to be represented by the law that generates it, by a stable structure, or* **by a computation the artefact performs** *— and E(G) is of the third kind.* *The Method 1.5 numbers-index.py* *and* *densities.py* *are named in the manifest as supporting sources and are absent, so the press prints a failure notice where the readout belongs.* **A readout that cannot run is a figure with no representation at all* **, which is the state §2.21 exists to forbid.*

DIGEST corrected on the point it got wrong: A CELL'S MEMBERS ARE ITS ROWS, and the `members` column is a COUNT of levels, not the levels — which is what made the first session read the collapse as irreversible. Two navigational facts written in because they cost this session a false negative and a wrong claim: `spectra_raw` CONTAINS A DIRECTORY, and M's T6 ruling that the store is authoritative with all three perspectives carried per cell.* **T9 OPENED AND MADE FIRST IN THE RESUMPTION ORDER: 68 series recovered no members and 128 recovered a count disagreeing with the store. 26% unexplained is not a residue, it is an unread finding, and calling it a residue would be the aesthetic deletion M refused at R 1662 wearing a different coat.** *T7's elaboration is recorded as OWED AND UNDELIVERED rather than quietly dropped — M asked for it, the session spent its budget elsewhere, and §H.0's lossy half-state is exactly what an unmarked omission would create.*

   534	### 1680
   535	
   536	**THE STORE IS INSIDE C3: `roundtrip.py` COVERS SIX ARTEFACTS, AND THE FIRST OF THEM IS NOT MARKDOWN.** *The standing carry-over — roundtrip covers five markdown artefacts and no TSV, which is why the store escaped C3 for as long as it did (R 1674) — is discharged. MEASUREMENTS.tsv stands where a hand-authored tail stands for the markdown artefacts: it is the authored input the generator does not write, so DECLARE names it and REFUSE removes it.* **6 of 6 round-trip, and 25/25 with the audit state cleared. DIFF: two consecutive runs byte-identical, and with no build date in the file the normalisation is a no-op, so the diff is unqualified. REFUSE: with MEASUREMENTS.tsv hidden the generator exits 1 and the artefact is unchanged by md5 — it writes nothing rather than a partial file.** *One repair not anticipated: promoting the new generator in place produced a CIRCULAR IMPORT, the replacement importing constants from the module it replaced. It failed loudly and at once, which is the good failure, but it is the shape of thing that passes silently when the import is soft. Constants and levels() inlined; `archive_store_gen_v1.py.bak` and `MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.v1.bak.tsv` held as evidence rather than deleted.* **WHAT T6 STILL DOES NOT COVER, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the generator closes the VALUE derivation and still INHERITS THE LIMIT ASSIGNMENT. R 1650's fallback — "else the first limit above its top member" — is what R 1664 voided on 145 rows, and a generator re-deriving limits would have to re-derive that and cannot: where a parent's limit was never published the series cannot be defected at all. That is T8, and it is now the ONLY part of the series construction left ungenerated.**

   541	
   542	**T10 OPENED — THE UNIQUENESS GUARD OF AUDIT 19 STOPS AT THREE DIGITS, AND TWO ENTRIES ARE DUPLICATED INSIDE THE RANGE IT CANNOT READ.** *Found while rebuilding the register after R 1683, not sought: REGISTER.md holds 1,478 headings and only 1,476 DISTINCT. Entries numbered 1215 and 1476 each appear TWICE, carrying different content in each instance — 1476 as two live figures disagreeing plus a fault in the gate meant to catch it, and separately as narration against computation over eighty-eight entries; 1215 as the spectra compendium rebuilt as a coordinate supply, and separately as Λ_spectra generated from bare nuclei. Both PRE-DATE this session; the seven entries written here, 1677 to 1683, are distinct and in order.* **THE GUARD IS `^ {0,3}((?:\d{3}, )*\d{3})\. ` — THREE DIGITS, EXACTLY. R 651 built it because two entries were both numbered 368 and no audit saw it. THE REGISTER PASSED 999 LONG AGO, so the guard covers R 165 to 999 and NOTHING AFTER, and the fault it was built to catch has recurred twice inside the blind range.** *And the same expression is SIMULTANEOUSLY TOO LOOSE: at R 1679 a wrapped line beginning " 358." inside an entry's PROSE impersonated an entry and failed the gate. So widening it to \d{3,4} without anchoring it against prose would trade a blind spot for a false-alarm rate already demonstrated to be non-hypothetical. THIS IS THE R 1671 SHAPE AGAIN — a check that could not fail in the direction it was pointed.* **REPAIR PROPOSED AND NOT APPLIED. Owner: M. A gate repair is not taken unilaterally, and §H.2.4 gives an unowned thread no standing.    684	### 1757
   685	
   686	**SIX HEADINGS HAD BEEN SILENT IN EVERY PRESS, THE CONTENTS WAS AN EMPTY FIELD, AND THE INDEX NOW PRINTS PAGE NUMBERS.** *Mapping the Index's locators to pages exposed both. Chapter 15's heading did not map because it did not exist in the pressed volume: in the source the line "## 15. Self-reference — alphabet, order, bounds" followed its previous paragraph with no blank line, so pandoc set it as running text — and the same held for the PART II heading, §8.1, §28.7.3, §28.7.8 and §31.2.1. Every earlier press was sampled and held, and the samples never fell on those six. Blank lines inserted; no other volume has the fault. The Contents: pandoc writes a table-of-contents field and the headless converter never populates it, so every pressed PDF to date has carried the heading "Table of Contents" over nothing — the sampled pages were always past it. Both are met by one press-time pass (`index_pages.py`, called by `build.py … pages`): press once, read each heading's page from the PDF, write a press-only copy of the source whose Contents block lists parts, chapters and appendices with their pages and whose Index carries a page after every § locator, press again, and repeat until the page map is stable — two re-presses at this build, 282 headings mapped, 308 locators resolved. The .md keeps its § locators, which are the source; the page numbers exist only in the pressed object, which is what a print index is. Main now presses at 274 pages with a real Contents on page 3.*

   690	### 1759
   691	
   692	**TWO HUNDRED AND SEVEN TABLES IN THE MAIN VOLUME HAD PRINTED AS RUN-ON PROSE IN EVERY PRESS, AND THE PRESS NOW SETS THEM.** *Found by sampling page 153 of the fresh press against Figure 24.1: §24.2's contributors table read "species core channels cells He I ²S 9 189 Ne I 2p⁵ ²P°, two limits 16 131 …" — one paragraph. The cause is the book's own dominant table form: a block indented two spaces with column alignment, which markdown treats as paragraph continuation and joins, while the press's display handling (1744) caught only four-space blocks. Two hundred and seven such blocks in the main volume — the principles table of Chapter 1, the kind table of Chapter 2, §24.1's spans, §24.2, B.3's flagged channels, the F.3 fibre table among them — three in the Spectra Compendium and two in the three-body paper; none in the Register, the other three compendia or the Löwdin paper. Every press to date carried them collapsed, and every sample happened to fall elsewhere — the same failure shape as 1757's six silent headings, and the same lesson as the audit that read the wrong artefact: the source was right, the object was wrong, and only reading the object at the defect found it. build.py's displays() now takes a block of two or three-space indented lines where at least half carry column alignment and sets it as the four-space blocks are set, literal spaces kept. Main re-pressed at 289 pages — the recovered tables claim fourteen pages — Spectra at 28, the paper at 10; the other five presses had no such blocks and stand.*

   696	### 1760
   697	
   698	**THE CITATION COUNTS ARE REFRESHED FROM THE FILES AND CHAT 8 CLOSES WITH THE CARRIED LIST EMPTY OF EVERYTHING THE RECORD COULD SETTLE.** *`register_cites.py` rerun over the record as it stands: 597 entries cited by other entries (was 593), 401 in the main volume, 721 with the compendia and papers, 1,012 with citations by entries; the load-bearing fifteen and every count in their table are unchanged, and every cited number has an entry. What remains open after this chat, and why: Q's standing items and item F's two retired generators are closed (1756); §34.4, §32.4.1, the Chapter 27 and Chapter 30 mislabels, the kinds table, F.1, the Register generator sentence, V14's six checks, the print index, the Contents, the He II series, ruling 23's caption, and the run-on tables are closed (1753–1759). Still the author's, because the record cannot decide them: whether §34.4's new body says what he meant the rule section to say; the F.4.2 definition of a surviving claim, which 297 entered in Q and which no computation supplies; and the 489 untested Spectra rows, which need the tolerance the builder does not state. Still the tool's nature rather than a defect: pressed page numbers exist only in the pressed object, and the two-space tables set in Georgia, not monospace, so their columns breathe — both stated where they occur.*

   702	### 1764
   703	
   704	**FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO CHANNEL ROWS OF THE SPECTRA COMPENDIUM HAD PRINTED AS LITERAL TEXT IN EVERY PRESS, AND THE PRESS NOW RE-HEADS THEM.** *Found by sampling the fresh press at the rows ruling 26 changed — the same lesson as 1757 and 1759 for the third time: the source was right, the object was wrong, and only reading the object at the change found it. The channel table is split by prose interjections — the He II note of 1758 among them — and each continuation block resumes with rows and no header line, which pandoc cannot set as a pipe table; from the interjection at the He II rows to the table's end, 532 rows printed as run-on text with their pipes literal, in this press and in every press before it, every earlier sample falling on the headed first block or on prose. The fix is the tool's, not the source's (1754's rule): build.py's new cont_tables() pass re-heads each headerless continuation block with its parent table's header and separator, guarded to blocks of two or more rows and four or more columns whose column count matches the parent, so a lone determinant or absolute-value line opening with a pipe stays text — the main volume's one such line does. One injection point recovers all 532 rows.*
   705	
   706	
   707	<!-- EXCISED 1766 : B-session -->
   708	### 1766
   709	
   710	**THE STATED REASON FOR THE FORTY-FIVE NO-DATA ROWS FALLS: "CAPTURES POST-DATE RESTORE-POINT-2_13" IS REFUTED IN WRITING — ALL SIX SPECIES WERE IN THE BANK, AND THE DELIVERY CARRIES THEM.** *The MANIFEST's Part B correction, verbatim: "'captures post-date restore-point-2_13' is REFUTED — all six species are in this bank as delivered here." 1763 printed the reason this corrects — that the 45 rows belong to Bi III, C I, Cd II, Hg II, N I and Sc III, "whose captures post-date the restore point and exist in no bank in reach" — and that sentence stands in 1763 as written, wrong in its reason and right in its status: the rows keep `untested`, but because the captures are unverified against their rows and unreconciled, not because they do not exist. The six captures are in the delivery under spectra_raw/ — BiIII_asd 2,370 bytes, CI_full 591, CdII_full 931, HgII_full 970, NI_full 698, ScIII_asd 1,269, each sha256-first-16 matched to the MANIFEST at fetch — and LIMITS-B.tsv, 155 bytes, extracted from channels.py's LIM, rides with them. The reason on the 45-row open item is now data in reach and unincorporated, not data that never existed; the item closes for an element only when its capture reconciles under the incorporation discipline. (a correction.)*

Three rulings were issued in this session (rulings 18–20): D.5.10's twelve fibre/coordinate assignments in Appendix D were confirmed by rerunning `dclose.py` (E = 0, nothing moves, register 1738); the `3B.shape` object was corrected from stale lines to its current state as the eighteenth root of the Mathematical Compendium, with the "fourteen roots" heading, the "248 objects · 17 roots" front line, and the "No new root" preamble all updated from current file information (register 1739); and all 27 Λ_phys dependence counts were regenerated on a single printed rule — seeds are objects whose statement names the parameter, count is transitive closure under the dependency graph — replacing 22 older counts that were never reproducible (register 1740). import re,json,collections
sites=json.load(open("EXCISE-SITES-BUILD14.json")); dang={int(k) for k in sites}
FILES={"MAIN":"The_Method_1_6-2.md","REGISTER":"The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md",
"MATH":"The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md","PHYS":"The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md",
"SPECTRA":"The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md","IOI":"The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md"}
rng=re.compile(r'(?i)\b(registers?)\s+((?:\d{3,4}(?:\s*[–\-]\s*\d{3,4})?)(?:\s*(?:,|and|/|;)\s*\d{3,4}(?:\s*[–\-]\s*\d{3,4})?)*)')
rr =re.compile(r'\b(R) ((?:\d{3,4}(?:\s*[–\-]\s*\d{3,4})?)(?:\s*(?:,|and|/|;)\s*\d{3,4}(?:\s*[–\-]\s*\d{3,4})?)*)')
firsthead=min(i for i,s in enumerate(open(FILES["REGISTER"],encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n"),1) if re.match(r"^### [\d,\s]+$",s))
exp=collections.defaultdict(list); zone=collections.Counter(); phr=0; allD=0; mix=0
for tag,fn in FILES.items():
    L=open(fn,encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n"); own=None
    for i,s in enumerate(L,1):
        if tag=="REGISTER":
            m=re.match(r"^### ([\d,\s]+?)\s*$",s)
            if m: own={int(x.strip()) for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip().isdigit()}; continue
        for pat in (rng,rr):
            for m in pat.finditer(s):
                parts=[p.strip() for p in re.split(r'\s*(?:,|and|/|;)\s*',m.group(2))]
                singles=[int(p) for p in parts if p.isdigit()]
                d=[n for n in singles if n in dang and not (tag=="REGISTER" and own and n in own)]
                if not d: continue
                phr+=1
                if len(d)==len(parts): allD+=1
                else: mix+=1
                z=("FRONT-MATTER" if i<firsthead else "ENTRY-BODY") if tag=="REGISTER" else "BOOK-PROSE"
                for n in d: exp[n].append((tag,i,z)); zone[z]+=1
print("EXPLICIT dangling pointers (ranges excluded):", sum(len(v) for v in exp.values()), "in", len(exp), "entries")
print("phrases to edit:",phr," all-dangling:",allD," mixed:",mix)
print("by zone:",dict(zone))
print("\nspan-only (no explicit pointer anywhere):", sorted(dang-set(exp)))
for n in sorted(exp): print(f"  {n:>5} x{len(exp[n])}  " + ",".join(f"{t}:{l}" for t,l,_ in exp[n]))
json.dump({str(k):v for k,v in sorted(exp.items())},open("POINTERS-BUILD14.json","w"),indent=1)
EOF

7 grouped headings carrying 32 numbers. No entry was added or removed this chat.

      There are FOURTEEN chats: Rebuild 1 … Rebuild 12, chat 13, chat 14. Read every summary.

      silently truncated on the first pass and had to be re-read by range. If the output
      shows "< truncated lines a-b >", the gate has NOT passed until those are read.
  G4  Print the certificate. Until it prints, state NOTHING about the work, change NO file.

  prompt rather than READ from a file, the gate has not passed.

                that does not come back byte-identical.

press_all.py, mkref.py, figs.py, pageproof.py, ratios.py, regsize.py, RESTORE-PACKS.md.
A directive naming a tool is not evidence the tool exists. M's chat-13 ruling on guard.py
stands verbatim in HANDOFF-15 §1.

"For all situations like this, please remover the pointers. As book project progresses the
prose will be corrected for coherence later on in one fell swoop once all the edits are done.
These edits we are doing are meant to be systematic because every edit changes each book
volume, and this each volume will be repeated edited throughout the project."

is removed wherever it stands, INCLUDING inside a live Register entry body. The clause's
CONTENT is kept. Prose coherence is NOT repaired site by site — it is swept later in one pass.
This overrides, for this class only, the standing "entry bodies are never edited" rule.
Rulings 1–26 are in HANDOFF-2/4/5/7/9/11; 27, 28 and the amendment are in WORKING-REGISTER.md.

By zone: 28 book prose · 3 Register front matter · 46 inside live Register entry bodies.

(bold, code-span, pipe and line counts unchanged in every file); and NO LIVE ENTRY LOST A
CITATION — recomputed against the .prepoint backups, the seventeen that fell are all absent.

**HANDOFF-15 §5 WAS WRONG TWICE AND BOTH FAULTS ARE WORTH CARRYING AS A CLASS.**
(i) Its line numbers were STALE. EXCISE-LIST.json predates W-001, which shifted the main
    volume ten lines; not one MAIN locator landed on its citation. A site list is a
    CONTENT claim; storing it as line numbers guarantees it rots at the next edit.
    EXCISE-LIST.json and EXCISE-LIST.md are now HISTORY. Do not use their locators.
(ii) It was SHORT BY TWELVE entries — 28 named against 40 real. register_cites.py gives 39,
    and misses 1732 because it parses ENTRY BODIES ONLY and 1732 is cited in the Register's
    FRONT MATTER. That is a live gap in the instrument, unrepaired, owner M.

**THE RULE THAT DECIDES WHAT IS A POINTER — needed again for every future excision.**
An explicit number naming an absent entry is a pointer and goes. A RANGE ("registers
1249–1357") names a SPAN, not an entry: it cannot be split, most members survive, and a
reader following it lands where it says. Ranges STAND. Measured: 18 ranges swallow an absent
number; 8 entries — 1149, 1257, 1358, 1386, 1388, 1389, 1667, 1668 — are reachable only by a
range and needed no edit. 97 sites = 77 explicit pointers (removed) + 20 span-only (stand).

Cause is chat 12's excision, confirmed by recomputing against the backups, not this chat's work.
  Register load-bearing table: 15 rows → 11. It named two ABSENT entries (1443 at 13×, 1650
    at 9×); 1526 and 1576 had fallen below the printed 7+ threshold because the entries citing
    them left in chat 12. Regenerated from the files.
  Register front matter: "597 entries are cited by other entries" → 556.
  Register front matter: 401 / 721 / 1,012 → 392 / 713 / 968, and its parenthetical from
    Build 9 to Build 15.
  MAIN: "the main volume cites 398 entries" → 392.
  build.py's press stamp: Build 9 — 2026-08-24 → Build 15 — 2026-08-25.
This is register 778's fault shape — a figure maintained in a second place — and it has now
reached the Register's OWN FRONT MATTER. Every future excision must drive these five sites.

build.py line 261: `if 'strip' in sys.argv: subprocess.run(['python3','appf.py',paged,'--write'])`.
So R1756's "Appendix F is recomputed at press" is TRUE ONLY WHEN THE PRESS IS INVOKED WITH THE
TOKEN `strip`. A press without it prints Appendix F from the source, and the source is stale:
it prints 1,532 distinct / 6,741 occurrences where appf.py now measures 1,525 / 6,729.

  F.1 distinct 1,527 → 1,525 · occurrences 6,735 → 6,729 · in tables 3,233 → 3,222

  F.4.2 ruled row UNCHANGED: withdrawn 1,447 · surviving 369 · 3.92 : 1 · p 0.203 · 0.728 bits
The ruled row not moving is the reassuring part — Ruling 25's census does not read prose
citations. Owner: M. The question is whether the gate should be removed so the recomputation
cannot be skipped, or whether a press without `strip` is a deliberate mode.

## 5. OPEN, IN ORDER, FOR CHAT 15
1. **THE PRESS. It is owed and it is first.** Six volumes changed this chat and NONE has been
   pressed. Press all six and SAMPLE THE PRESSED OBJECT AT THE CHANGED SITES — the 77 pointer
   removals, the regenerated load-bearing table, the four count sentences. Include inside the
   Spectra Part II continuation blocks (the R1764 fault). Pass `strip` (see §4).
   This project's record says three times — 1757, 1759, 1764 — that the source was right and
   the object was wrong, and only reading the object AT THE CHANGE found it.
2. Phase 2 reader audits, one volume per segment, against the compendium gold standard.
3. Ruling 29's coherence sweep is M's, later, in one pass. Do not start it site by site.

## 6. DO NOT START WITHOUT M's RULING
- The 126 unreconciled Spectra rows.
- The five narrow-bracket FAIL rows named in R1763.

- The 1,447 / 1,472 count question (HELD by M at PR1 — report if it moves, do not re-ask).

Reading it cold, as a reader rather than the person who has been counting its numbers:

**Appendix F is where the book turns its own instrument on itself in the one place it actually costs something.**

The book indexes and closes things — mathematics in D, ignorance in E, errors in Chapter 28, terms in the Index. Those are all domains the method can win in. F indexes the book's *arithmetic*, and the answer comes back badly: 79% of the numbers printed here sit at the weakest verification the coordinate admits. F.3.1 says plainly that this isn't a claim 79% are wrong — it's a measurement of how much of the book stands on the reader's trust rather than on the book's own standard.

That's the purpose. **It converts the book's most obvious objection from something a reviewer says into something the book measures.** §32.1.1's referee flag 4 — the register is longer than the results — becomes 1.73 in F.4.1. "Take my word for it" becomes 79%.

**F.3.3 is the section that earns the appendix.** It notices that a count of what the book omits, computed from the book, moves when you write the count down — E(G) read 33, 38, 24, 23, 21 in one session, every move caused by the writing. Rather than picking a number, it derives what's actually stable: the constraint, the three refutations, the nine admitted-and-absent combinations. The count demotes itself to a press readout, "a readout, not a claim." That's the book's own law-versus-extent rule applied reflexively and surviving the application. If someone wanted one section to decide whether this method is real or decorative, I'd point them there.

**Where I'd push back as a reader.** F.5 is n = 8. F.4.1 concedes a ratio with one observation is a number, not a trend. So the appendix mostly *installs* instruments and reports first readings — it's constitutional rather than evidential. And there's a real risk it reads as the book grading its own homework and taking credit for the candour. The defence against that is F.5's falsification and F.3.2's tripwire — but F.3.2 openly says the failure threshold is a decision you haven't made, and an alarm with no threshold can't go off. That's honest, and it's also the softest point in the appendix.

One thing from this session bears directly on it: the readout F.3.3 calls the honest representation only runs when the press is invoked with `strip`. The appendix's central move depends on a computation that can silently not happen.

11311	### F.3.1 And the distribution is the finding
 11312	 Of 6,741 indexed occurrences at this press, **5,311 carry verification = asserted** — no recomputation recorded
 11313	 anywhere near them — against 601 recomputed and 829 recomputed under variation. On the definition
 11314	 axis, 5,590 are asserted, 642 stated, and 509 stated with their inputs (first reading: 2,316 of 2,453
 11315	 asserted, 115 and 22; definition 1,998 / 145 / 310). So 79% — 94% at the first reading — of the numbers this
 11316	 book prints are, by its own coordinates, at the weakest verification the coordinate admits. That is
 11317	 not a claim that 79% are wrong. It is a measurement of how much of the book's arithmetic stands on
 11318	 the reader's trust rather than on the book's own standard, and it is the first time the quantity has
 11319	 had a number.
 11320	
 11321	### F.3.2 The tripwire
 11322	 The press runs the extraction on every render and reports the count before any reading — a D1-type
 11323	 check in Chapter 16's sense: mechanical, prior, and indifferent to what the author believes. It
 11324	 reports and does not fail the build, because a failing build on 94% would stop the book from printing
 11325	 at all. The threshold is a decision the author has not made, and recording that it is undecided is
 11326	 better than choosing it silently.
 11327	
 11328	### F.3.3 The closure, represented as it must be
 11329	 A count of what this book omits is computed **from** this book, so writing the count into the book
 11330	 changes what it counts. E(G) read 33, 38, 24, 23 and 21 within one session and every move was caused
 11331	 by the writing. **The count is the wrong representation, and it is wrong for a reason the book already
 11332	 states.**
 11333	
 11334	 §12.11.3.1 divides bounds by where they come from. **A bound from a law is stable; a bound from an
 11335	 extent moves with the extent.** E(G) is an extent quantity — of course it moves. What is law-derived
 11336	 here does not move, and measured across three states of the book, one before the third companion
 11337	 paper's intake, one before the register was compressed, and one now:
 11338	
 11339	  what is asserted                                                          before intake   before compression   now
 11340	  E(G), the count                                                                      23                   21    23
 11341	  **the constraint** — definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated               holds                holds  holds
 11342	  **the three refutations** — recomputed ⇏ stated, ⇏ enumerated, ⇏ both              hold                 hold   hold
 11343	  **combinations admitted and absent** — nine of an eleven-element union             all nine             all nine  all nine
 11344	
 11345	 **So the closure is represented by three things, and the count is not one of them.**
 11346	
 11347	    **First, the constraint**, which is a fact about F.3's assignment rules and cannot be made false
 11348	    by writing: *definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated*. **Second, the three refutations**,
 11349	    which are facts about what the book already prints and would need a withdrawal to overturn.
 11350	    **Third, the nine combinations** that stand admitted and absent in every state of the book —
 11351	    these are the shape of the omission, and they are what a reader should be given.
 11352	
 11353	 The nine are: a number **recomputed while its definition is only asserted**, at each of the three input
 11354	 standards; a number recomputed **under variation** with its definition asserted, at two of them; and a
 11355	 number whose definition is *stated* or *stated with inputs* while its inputs are **printed**, at each
 11356	 verification level. Two further combinations come and go with the text and are named as unstable
 11357	 rather than counted.
 11358	
 11359	 **The count remains, printed by the press at each build rather than by the author** — a readout, not
 11360	 a claim. **This is the law–extent rule turned on the book's own index**: state what the rules forbid
 11361	 and what the extent has refuted, and let the extent's own arithmetic be computed rather than written.
 11362	 Register 370.
 11363	
 11364	### F.4 What closing it would establish, and what it costs
 11365	 D.6 claims nothing is missing that the structure admits, about the book's mathematics. Closing G
 11366	 extends that from the mathematics to the arithmetic, and makes §32.2's S3 — that a reader given the
 11367	 claims and the evidence could reconstruct the structure — true in the strong sense rather than the
 11368	 prose one. The cost is E.4-shaped: buildable, days to unbounded, depends = no. Entered in Q as
 11369	 item M, enumerated rather than asserted away.
 11370	
 11371	### F.4.1 Two ratios the book had never measured about itself
 11372	 Appendix F indexes the numbers this book prints and had not indexed the two that describe its own
 11373	 shape. They are named here because a quantity without a name cannot be tracked, and both are
 11374	 measurements the method demands of anything else it examines.
 11375	
 11376	    **The withdrawal ratio.** Words of register against words of argument — Chapter 28 against every other chapter of the book. **0.445 when first measured (register 296), 0.249 after the register was compressed
 11377	, and a press readout since register 374.** Those readings were taken while the entries lived inside Chapter 28. The Register is now its own volume, so the ratio has two readings and the book prints both, dated: **Chapter 28 against every other chapter, 5,704: 108,630 = 0.053**, which measures only the chapter that discusses the withdrawals; and **the Register volume against the main volume, 197,651: 114,334 = 1.73**, which is the like-for-like successor of 0.445 and 0.249 (both recomputed 2026-08-24 from the files). At the second reading the record is larger than the argument, and that is stated rather than hidden in a chapter count.
 11378	
 11379	    **The method ratio.** Words of Part I — the twenty principles, the twenty-four protocols,
 11380	    the twenty-two prime audits — against the whole book but for itself. **12,663 : 101,671 = 0.125** (2026-08-24; 11,811 : 75,459 = 0.157 when first measured). Against the
 11381	    six appendices alone it is 0.800: the machinery is now very nearly the size of all the
 11382	    mathematics it audits.
 11383	
 11384	 **What each is for.** §32.1.1's fourth referee flag says the register is longer than the results and
 11385	 the book has no answer to the fair version of the question. The withdrawal ratio is that question
 11386	 made numeric: at 0.249 the register was a quarter of the argument and at 1.73 it is larger than the argument, and the flag asked not whether that is

### F.3.1 And the distribution is the finding
 Of 6,741 indexed occurrences at this press, **5,311 carry verification = asserted** — no recomputation recorded
 anywhere near them — against 601 recomputed and 829 recomputed under variation. On the definition
 axis, 5,590 are asserted, 642 stated, and 509 stated with their inputs (first reading: 2,316 of 2,453
 asserted, 115 and 22; definition 1,998 / 145 / 310). So 79% — 94% at the first reading — of the numbers this
 book prints are, by its own coordinates, at the weakest verification the coordinate admits. That is
 not a claim that 79% are wrong. It is a measurement of how much of the book's arithmetic stands on
 the reader's trust rather than on the book's own standard, and it is the first time the quantity has
 had a number.

### F.3.2 The tripwire
 The press runs the extraction on every render and reports the count before any reading — a D1-type
 check in Chapter 16's sense: mechanical, prior, and indifferent to what the author believes. It
 reports and does not fail the build, because a failing build on 94% would stop the book from printing
 at all. The threshold is a decision the author has not made, and recording that it is undecided is
 better than choosing it silently.

### F.3.3 The closure, represented as it must be
 A count of what this book omits is computed **from** this book, so writing the count into the book
 changes what it counts. E(G) read 33, 38, 24, 23 and 21 within one session and every move was caused
 by the writing. **The count is the wrong representation, and it is wrong for a reason the book already
 states.**

 §12.11.3.1 divides bounds by where they come from. **A bound from a law is stable; a bound from an
 extent moves with the extent.** E(G) is an extent quantity — of course it moves. What is law-derived
 here does not move, and measured across three states of the book, one before the third companion
 paper's intake, one before the register was compressed, and one now:

  what is asserted                                                          before intake   before compression   now
  E(G), the count                                                                      23                   21    23
  **the constraint** — definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated               holds                holds  holds
  **the three refutations** — recomputed ⇏ stated, ⇏ enumerated, ⇏ both              hold                 hold   hold
  **combinations admitted and absent** — nine of an eleven-element union             all nine             all nine  all nine

 **So the closure is represented by three things, and the count is not one of them.**

    **First, the constraint**, which is a fact about F.3's assignment rules and cannot be made false
    by writing: *definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated*. **Second, the three refutations**,
    which are facts about what the book already prints and would need a withdrawal to overturn.
    **Third, the nine combinations** that stand admitted and absent in every state of the book —
    these are the shape of the omission, and they are what a reader should be given.

 The nine are: a number **recomputed while its definition is only asserted**, at each of the three input
 standards; a number recomputed **under variation** with its definition asserted, at two of them; and a
 number whose definition is *stated* or *stated with inputs* while its inputs are **printed**, at each
 verification level. Two further combinations come and go with the text and are named as unstable
 rather than counted.

 **The count remains, printed by the press at each build rather than by the author** — a readout, not
 a claim. **This is the law–extent rule turned on the book's own index**: state what the rules forbid
 and what the extent has refuted, and let the extent's own arithmetic be computed rather than written.

Reading it cold, as a reader rather than the person who has been counting its numbers:

**Appendix F is where the book turns its own instrument on itself in the one place it actually costs something.**

The book indexes and closes things — mathematics in D, ignorance in E, errors in Chapter 28, terms in the Index. Those are all domains the method can win in. F indexes the book's *arithmetic*, and the answer comes back badly: 79% of the numbers printed here sit at the weakest verification the coordinate admits. F.3.1 says plainly that this isn't a claim 79% are wrong — it's a measurement of how much of the book stands on the reader's trust rather than on the book's own standard.

That's the purpose. **It converts the book's most obvious objection from something a reviewer says into something the book measures.** §32.1.1's referee flag 4 — the register is longer than the results — becomes 1.73 in F.4.1. "Take my word for it" becomes 79%.

**F.3.3 is the section that earns the appendix.** It notices that a count of what the book omits, computed from the book, moves when you write the count down — E(G) read 33, 38, 24, 23, 21 in one session, every move caused by the writing. Rather than picking a number, it derives what's actually stable: the constraint, the three refutations, the nine admitted-and-absent combinations. The count demotes itself to a press readout, "a readout, not a claim." That's the book's own law-versus-extent rule applied reflexively and surviving the application. If someone wanted one section to decide whether this method is real or decorative, I'd point them there.

**Where I'd push back as a reader.** F.5 is n = 8. F.4.1 concedes a ratio with one observation is a number, not a trend. So the appendix mostly *installs* instruments and reports first readings — it's constitutional rather than evidential. And there's a real risk it reads as the book grading its own homework and taking credit for the candour. ## 2A. RULING 30 — APPENDIX F IS REMOVED (author, chat 14, verbatim)
"Appendix f will have to be completely rebuilt from scratch because it was built to include
things that I have since ruled against. And that's okay. This is part of the editorial process.
But appendix F will continue to cause problems until we address it. My instructions for the
next chat ... are to completely remove appendix f without objection, but leave a placeholder so
any reference to appendix f doesn't trigger a fault or flag, and schedule it's complete rebuild
for between the edit and audit phases of the project."

**EXECUTE WITHOUT OBJECTION. Do not re-argue it, do not ask for it to be confirmed, do not
preserve parts of it on the ground that they seem worth keeping.** The reasoning is settled and
is recorded here so no session needs to reconstruct it: Appendix F indexes the book's OWN
printed numbers and reports how well the book verified itself — 79% asserted, a withdrawal
ratio, a sample of eight. Under the Ruling 27 Amendment, verifying "the truth of a number the
books state" is EDITORIAL and irrelevant to a reader. F predates that amendment. It is the
largest surviving instance of the class chat 12 excised, and it sits in the book.

WHAT THE REBUILD IS FOR, so it is not lost: the two things in F that are METHOD rather than
self-audit are (a) §F.2's four coordinates — quantity-kind fibred over definition < inputs <
verification, each ordered — which is an index construction over a new domain, and (b) §F.3.3's
argument that a self-count is unstable by construction, so a closure must be represented by its
constraint and its refutations rather than by its count. Those are the seed of the rebuild.
They are NOT to be salvaged into the placeholder; the rebuild starts from scratch.

SCHEDULED: the rebuild sits BETWEEN the edit phase and the audit phase. It is not chat 15's
work and it is not part of Phase 2. Do not begin it early.

## 2B. THE REMOVAL — MEASURED THIS CHAT, DO NOT RE-DERIVE
Extent: **main volume lines 11208–11497, 290 lines**, from `## Appendix F — The numbers,
indexed` to the line before `# END MATTER`. The contents block carries a second heading at
**line 168** — the body heading is the LAST occurrence, the contents entry the first. Match by
content, never by position; the file will have moved by the time this is read.

**79 references stand OUTSIDE the appendix body and must not fault: MAIN 50, REGISTER 29.**
They are of four shapes, and the placeholder has to satisfy all four:
  - `Appendix F` by name (contents block, Q item M at ~L10941, §D/E cross-references)
  - `§F.n.n` locators — §F.3.3 is cited three times in Chapter 2 alone, at ~L1081/1092/1096,
    where it is load-bearing for the by-the-law / by-the-stable-structure distinction
  - bare `F.4.1`, `F.4.2` in the Register's own entries — those are RECORD and are not touched
  - `E(G)`, the open count, named in the main volume's press-readout sentences (~L857, L1102)
**The Register's 29 are entry bodies and stay as written.** History stands (§H.4). Only the
main volume's live prose needs the placeholder to resolve against.

INSTRUMENTS: `appf.py` (12 references) becomes dead code — RETIRE it, do not delete it, and
say so in the placeholder's own note. `build.py` line 261 calls it behind the `strip` token
(§4); that call must go with it or the press will fail on a missing section.

THE PLACEHOLDER must (i) keep a `## Appendix F` heading so the contents and every by-name
reference resolve, (ii) carry section anchors for every §F.n.n cited elsewhere in the main
volume — at minimum F.2 and F.3.3 — so no locator dangles, (iii) state in one short paragraph
that the appendix is withdrawn pending rebuild and why, and (iv) print no number, since a
number is what the ruling removes. **The removal is a change to a volume, so it is recorded —
in WORKING-REGISTER.md as W-003, not in the Register: it is editorial by Ruling 27.**

## 5. OPEN, IN ORDER, FOR CHAT 15
